classification.difficultyReason: Determine the mean, amplitude and full period from temperature extrema six months apart, with time starting at the maximum.

content.prompt:
The average daily temperature in a rural town has a maximum of $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ on January 23. The average daily temperature for the town has a minimum of $13^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and this occurs six months later.

Let $t$ be the time in months after January 23. Find a function of the form
$$T(t)=a\cos(nt)+b$$
to model the daily average temperature $T$ in the town at time $t$.

answer.short: $T(t)=6\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)+19$, where $t$ is measured in months and $T$ in $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
answer.worked:
The mean temperature is $19^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and the amplitude is $6^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The maximum occurs at $t=0$, so the cosine coefficient is positive. Six months is half a period; the full period is 12 months.
$$\begin{align*}
a&=\frac{25-13}{2}\\
a&=6\\
b&=\frac{25+13}{2}\\
b&=19\\
n&=\frac{2\pi}{12}\\
n&=\frac{\pi}{6}\\
T(t)&=6\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)+19.
\end{align*}$$
Here $t$ is measured in months and $T(t)$ in $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
